sessions.task: Map vs gate: 'Where may I legally put an ImageTexture?'

steps.text: Task: 'Where may I legally put an ImageTexture?' Legal means the gate (X3DUOM acceptableNodeTypes, then XSD), not the ontology. Plan: ask the ontology map first (node_parents) to see what it proposes, then where_can_place, then ontology_vs_gate to line them up with XSD verdicts.

The map proposes 63 rows, and about half are hasChildren of audio and grouping nodes (Gain, Analyser, Scene, StaticGroup...): an ImageTexture is not an X3DChildNode, so these come from a pooled range, not from a real slot. It also mixes naming (TextureProjector 'texture' without has-) and does not say which ontology release it read. Now the gate: where_can_place.

Gate: 36 (parent, field) rows on the X3DUOM 4.1, every one a texture-shaped slot, with containerField needed everywhere except Appearance.texture, MultiTexture, ComposedTexture3D and the TextureProjectors. It also has slots the map lacks (GeoMetadata.data, LoadSensor.children, OpacityMapVolumeStyle.transferFunction). Now line the three answers up with ontology_vs_gate, XSD on.

Counts on the 4.1 map vs gate: map 85 (parent, field) pairs over 62 parents (55 concrete), gate 36 pairs over 14 parents, 12 parents in both, 50 map-only, 2 gate-only. XSD: gate pairs 31 A, 4 I, 1 R; map-only pairs 42 R, 2 I. node_parents (call 1) gave 63 rows because it read the 4.0 release by default. Four gate pairs are I (harness could not tell). I can settle two of them myself: a minimal document with ComposedTexture3D.texture and OpacityMapVolumeStyle.transferFunction, through validate_x3d.

steps.text: Legal homes for an ImageTexture in an X3D 4.1 XML document (gate admits it AND the XSD accepts): 31 (parent, field) slots on 10 parents. Without a containerField attribute: Appearance.texture, MultiTexture.texture, TextureProjector.texture, TextureProjectorParallel.texture. With containerField set: Material ambient/diffuse/emissive/normal/occlusion/shininess/specularTexture; PhysicalMaterial base/emissive/metallicRoughness/normal/occlusionTexture; UnlitMaterial emissive/normalTexture; ComposedCubeMapTexture and TextureBackground back/bottom/front/left/right/topTexture; LoadSensor children (as a watched url object). The gate also lists 5 slots the XSD did not accept in my probes or its table: GeoMetadata.data, OpacityMapVolumeStyle.transferFunction, BlendedVolumeStyle.weightTransferFunction1/2 (containerField enumeration) and ComposedTexture3D.texture (content model wants a MovieTexture); validate_semantic is silent on those, so only validate_x3d catches them. Why the answers differ: the ontology map proposes 85 pairs on 62 parents because one property, hasChildren, carries the pooled ranges of every children field; its range X3DUrlObject (from LoadSensor's watch list) subsumes ImageTexture, so every grouping and audio node appears to accept one. That is a proposal, not a verdict: the XSD rejects 42 of the 50 map-only pairs and could not test 2. Rule of thumb: ask where_can_place, then validate_x3d; never place by node_parents. steps.text: Two traps in that answer: rdf:rest*/rdf:first returns a set, so Pearl's (1 1 1) collapses to '1', and component order is lost (Cobalt reads 0.95 0.28 0.12, surely reversed). steps.text: Recommendation: keep reasoning at 'subclass' (the default) for questions, and OFF (inference='none') for validation. Do not turn on rdfs or owl-rl for this ontology except to study the ontology itself. The numbers on the Cabinet (1939 triples): subclass adds 579 rdf:type triples and gives each node 3 to 7 types, all true superclasses (a Sphere is also an X3DGeometryNode and an X3DNode), in 0.6 s. rdfs adds 64,764 triples (84,811 total) and gives a median node 347 types (max 355), in 15 s. owl-rl adds 95,182 (115,229 total), same type counts, in 50 s. Why it explodes: the ontology records 'which node types have this field' as a list of rdfs:domain classes (294 of 901 such properties list more than one class; DEF lists 337). RDFS and OWL read several domains as all applying at once, so any node with a DEF is inferred to be an Analyser, an Anchor, an Appearance... at the same time. This is consistent rather than an error, because the ontology declares no disjointness. It also changes verdicts: on a probe with a Box wrongly placed in Transform.children, SHACL without inference reports exactly that one Violation; with rdfs it reports 807 results (804 field-domain Violations, 3 'Shape has no geometry' Warnings on a Box, a Transform and a Viewpoint), and the real Violation disappears. Reasoning both hid the true error and invented hundreds of false ones. With inference on, the Cabinet-sized scene could not even be checked within the server's 20 s deadline. The ontology proposes, the shapes dispose, the validators gate: reason over class membership, then validate without inference. Receipts: 5 claims, ledger verified, 31 records, head 63ca0e0d...

sessions.outcome: Recommendation: subclass for questions, none for validation; rdfs and owl-rl only to study the ontology. subclass +579 type triples (3/6/7 types per node); rdfs +64,764 (median 347 types); owl-rl +95,182 (50 s). With rdfs, a probe's one real SHACL Violation vanished under 807 spurious results; with inference on, a Cabinet-sized scene does not finish inside the 20 s deadline. 5 claims; final ledger 31 records, verified.
